name: Ransalu Senanayake
title: Assistant Professor; LENS Lab Principal Investigator
department: School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence
fitReason: Strong physical-AI match in evaluating, improving and diagnosing learned robot policies, with an explicit outside-ASU visitor inquiry route.

physicalEvidence.summary: Vantage v2 (October 2025) reports actual Unitree D1 seven-DoF arm reaching with an ACT visuomotor policy. Bayesian optimization selects a camera view for policy fine-tuning; physical success is 44%, versus 30–36% viewpoint-randomization baselines. RoboSuite manipulation, diffusion-policy results and injected camera-placement noise are simulation. The paper explicitly affiliates all authors with LENS/ASU; current lab roster lists coauthors Sreevishakh V as an MS student and Som Sagar as a PhD student, establishing directed-group linkage. May 2026 RoboMD adds failure-diagnosis work involving UR5e and SO101; its diagnostic RL operates in an embedding space, not as a low-level movement policy.

shortVisit.summary: Current outside-ASU visitor form explicitly includes master’s students. The lab cannot host visitors without their own funding. Duration, onsite arrangements, summer 2027 capacity and approved institutional appointment remain unconfirmed.

scoreReasons.fit: Substantive learned visuomotor adaptation and reliability research in manipulation.
scoreReasons.physical: Named executed ACT robot study with current LENS student authors and explicit LENS affiliation; simulation results kept separate.

name: Nicola Bezzo
title: Associate Professor; Autonomous Mobile Robots Lab Director
fitReason: Strong safe-learning/control match with learned safety adaptation actually executed on ground robots, rather than simulation-only RL.

physicalEvidence.summary: ICRA 2025 primary paper reports a Soft Actor-Critic policy adapting the barrier parameter of an MPC safety constraint during actual Clearpath Jackal clutter navigation and Boston Dynamics Spot office-corridor navigation. Training uses Gazebo; physical trials use the pretrained policy without online weight retraining. Numerical success-rate table is simulation, not physical evaluation. Lead author Nick Mohammad is listed as the lab’s 2026 PhD alumnus and experimental helper Woosung Kim is a current PhD student; current lab research page claims this project. Dynamic-obstacle handling is future work.

shortVisit.summary: Current AMR research page welcomes general emails about working together, but does not specify outside-master visitors, short stays or summer 2027. No qualifying lab-level external short-visit invitation verified.

scoreReasons.fit: Substantive neural SAC adaptation integrated with actual safe navigation control.
scoreReasons.physical: Named hardware trials in a current-lab project with own PhD author and current experimental contributor.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Only a generic research-interest contact; external short-visitor arrangement remains unknown.
scoreReasons.freshness: Official January 2026 robotics program lists a talk and demonstrations, and roster includes 2026 graduate; detailed safe-RL hardware study is 2025.
